subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: Randomized Controlled Trials: The Gold Standard
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Randomized Controlled Trials: The Gold Standard.

hook.text: James Lind gave some sailors oranges & others vinegar in 1747. The orange group didn't get scurvy.

buildup.text: RCTs: randomly assign people to treatment or control groups, apply the intervention, measure the difference.

discovery.text: Randomization eliminates confounding variables — differences between groups are due to chance, not hidden factors.

twist.text: But RCTs can't test everything. You can't randomly assign people to 'smoking' or 'non-smoking' groups for 30 years.

climax.text: Double-blinding (neither participants nor researchers know who gets what) prevents placebo effects and researcher bias.

punchline.text: The best way to test a cause: change one thing, randomize everything else.

quiz.question: Why is randomization essential in clinical trials?
options: It eliminates confounding variables between groups

details.summary: Randomized controlled trials randomly assign participants to treatment or control groups, isolating the variable being tested. This design eliminates confounding factors that plague observational studies.
details.whyItMatters: RCTs are the gold standard for establishing causation because randomization ensures that differences in outcomes are caused by the treatment, not hidden variables.
takeaways: Control groups isolate the effect of the treatment
Double-blinding prevents placebo and observer bias

faq.question: Why is randomization so important in controlled trials?
faq.answer: Randomization ensures treatment and control groups are statistically identical in all respects except the treatment. Without it, pre-existing differences between groups could explain the results instead of the treatment itself.

faq.question: When are randomized controlled trials not possible or ethical?
faq.answer: You cannot randomly assign people to smoke for 20 years or live in poverty. When the treatment would be harmful or unethical, researchers must use observational studies and natural experiments, accepting their limitations.
